title: Surrender
tomorrow: Pop calls the cane one more thing to wear. what goes on last?

lines: PLEASE FIX IT. WHATEVER YOU WANT.
NIGHT, ON THE MOUNT OF OLIVES.
cards: Can you pray please fix it and whatever you want in the same breath? Jesus did. Night on the Mount of Olives.
He tells his friends to pray, goes on about a stone's cast, and kneels. And the first thing he asks for is honest, and very human: that what's coming might not come.

teach.h: HE ASKS FIRST: REMOVE THIS CUP.
teach.b: Luke gives the prayer: “Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.” The cup is the suffering ahead. Notice the order.
He asks first, and he means it. Surrender here isn't pretending not to want anything. It's saying plainly what you want, then letting go of the outcome.
The hinge is one word: nevertheless.

Mark keeps the word Jesus opened with, Abba, the family word for father, so the letting go happens inside trust, not fear. And it echoes a prayer he taught his followers in daylight: thy will be done.
Now look back at the week, because surrender gathers it up. Gratitude turns back. Joy feasts after tears.
Contentment stays steady. Patience waits and keeps tending.
Courage takes one step in company. Hope holds out of sight. Each one asks honestly for something, then opens its hands.
Christians describe this scene in different words: obedience, trust, or simply yes.

how: Christians pray 'thy will be done' in the Lord's Prayer, and some recall Jesus' prayer on the Mount of Olives when facing outcomes they cannot control; some pray it with open hands.

o: losing an argument and admitting you were wrong
saying what you want, then trusting God with the outcome
giving up on what you want and not caring at all

games.q: the week of the heart — tap the pairs.

s: Paul says to give thanks for every thing
“in every thing give thanks”: thanks inside hard times, not for them.
Mark records Jesus beginning the prayer with 'Abba'
“Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee.”
James's farmer stops tending the field while he waits for rain
he waits with long patience, and keeps working.

games.q: a friend's dad just lost his job. she says, 'i'm just going to accept it and not ask God for anything.' what does the prayer on the Mount of Olives suggest?
o: ask honestly for what you want, then trust God with the outcome.
never ask; real surrender means wanting nothing at all.
keep demanding until it changes, and don't let go.
games.why: Jesus asked first, “remove this cup from me,” and then said “nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.” the ask comes before the letting go.

practice: Name one outcome you're gripping: a result, a reply, someone else's choice. Say honestly, in your head, what you want.
Then turn your hands palms up on your knees and rest them there; if you pray, you can use his words: not my will, but thine, be done.

wordCard.voice: Surrender. Saying honestly what you want, then letting go of the outcome in trust.

orig.note: Greek for 'will,' in 'not my will' and in 'thy will be done.'

carryVoice: Your line: thy will. Said after an honest ask, not instead of one. Seven days of the heart, done.

sources.q: Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me: nevertheless not my will, but thine, be done.
Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee
